bluf: iPullRank is a US, founder led AI search agency, Mike King as founder, selling relevance engineering, GEO, technical SEO, content and generative AI programs to enterprise and mid market brands, priced in three productized readiness tiers with no prices shown. It is doing AI search as the whole pitch: the AI Search Manual, webinars, 150 AI topic URLs and 24+ LinkedIn ads telling CMOs that AI search is deciding which brands lead. The record shows no dated move. The thing a rival should know: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt, its sitemap has 0 updates in 90 days, and no client is named anywhere in the record.
doing:
iPullRank positions itself as an enterprise and mid market AI search agency applying relevance engineering and resonance design so AI recommends brands and people remember them. In plain words: a technical SEO shop that has renamed its method for the answer engine era and sells it as an engineering discipline rather than a channel. Its headline claim is $5B+ in client results, including $2.4B in incremental revenue for one of the world's largest banks, quoted as its claim; the bank is not named.

The sold mix leads with AI search and GEO (scored 3: the homepage title calls it an AI search agency, a GEO service, the AI Search Manual, a self storage AI Overview case) and SEO (scored 3: the meta leads with enterprise SEO, a technical SEO service covering JavaScript SEO and migrations, bank and car publisher SEO cases). Behind them sit AI automation (scored 2: a generative AI service that builds custom AI content programs and prompt libraries, with an AI content case citing $290M in revenue) and content and digital PR (scored 2: content strategy and marketing on its Resonance Design approach, plus content engineering). Every media, CRM, web and commerce line scores 0, so breadth is 5. Proprietary: Relevance Engineering, Resonance Design, the AI Search Manual and an AI Search Readiness assessment. No partners are listed.

AI posture: AI search is the headline offer, with custom generative AI content programs built for clients alongside it. The moves list is empty and no news, case studies or jobs were captured. Pricing signals: productized rather than hourly, three readiness tiers named Emerging, Growth and Enterprise with scoped deliverables, and no prices shown. Conspicuously absent for an AI search agency of its kind: any audited AI visibility product (tracking, scorecard, citation share), any feed, schema or entity service line, any named client, and llms.txt on its own site.
clients:
The record types the client as enterprise, with the positioning line adding mid market, across banking and financial services, mortgage, ecommerce and marketplaces, media and publishing, telecom, self storage and automotive. The home market is the US; no office city is listed.

The needs read is empty: 0 clients, 0 observed, 0 named only, no mix and no shared clients, because the case pages the record indexes describe clients by category rather than name. What the capability notes and claims do describe, unnamed: one of the world's largest banks credited with $2.4B in incremental revenue and a bank SEO case (organic demand, observed as a claim), a car publisher SEO case (organic demand), a self storage AI Overview case (AI and automation, the AI search visibility need), and an AI content case citing $290M in revenue (AI and automation plus content). These are engagements without a client name, the reverse of the usual names only problem, so nothing can be marked shared with another tracked agency and nothing can be checked with the client.

openings:
The strongest opening is the audited number. iPullRank sells AI visibility as relevance engineering, but the record shows no audited AI visibility product (tracking, scorecard, citation share) and no llms.txt on its own site despite 150 AI topic URLs. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival leading with a measured citation share and a published llms.txt takes the enterprise RFP where the buyer asks how the result is counted. Falsifier: an iPullRank scorecard or citation share product appearing on its capabilities pages.

Second, the idle house: 0 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days from an agency that sells content engineering, which a rival with a live cadence can state flatly. Third, no feed, schema or entity work on a core search line leaves the machine readable layer unclaimed. Fourth, pricing: it already sells productized tiers, so a rival cannot beat it on transparency alone and must price on the outcome, the citation, not the tier. Fifth, proof: no client is named in the record, so the $5B+ and $2.4B claims cannot be checked with a buyer. The Monsoon read at 58.1 with an observed hourly term says an offshore delivered SEO line can undercut the technical SEO retainers.
